name: Reconcile page
description: Two sets of records that ought to agree, with the difference between them written out as a figure and the controls that make them agree — pairing, explaining and posting. The variance is the content; the rows that already agree are a count.
when_to_use: Two populations of records that are supposed to say the same thing and somebody accountable for the fact that they do not: a purchase order against a goods receipt against the vendor's invoice, a bank statement against the ledger, a physical stock count against the system quantity. The test is that both sides already exist and both are true — reconciliation is an agreement between records that have already been written, and the work is finding the pairs and explaining the gaps. compare-page looks almost identical and is the opposite job: several vendors' quotations laid out side by side so somebody can choose one, where the columns are candidates rather than facts and the outcome is a decision rather than an entry. If the columns are things you are choosing between, that is compare-page; if they are things that have already happened and disagree, it is this. A column that sums at the foot of one table is not a screen at all — that is table's totals variant, a region inside a page. And where the variance is a fact somebody is reading about one record rather than the work in front of them — an order that says 4 of 9 lines received — it belongs on record-page beside the rest of the record, not on a screen of its own. index-page is the register scanned and filtered, list-detail is the queue worked one record at a time with the record beside it; this is neither, because the unit of work here is a pair rather than a record.
rules: The variance is the whole page and the agreement is a count. Two columns of matching rows are not information — the four lines that disagree are the reason anybody opened this screen, so they render first, at full size, and the twelve that agree collapse to one strip saying how many and what they came to. The rejected alternative is one table of all sixteen lines with the four scattered through it, which turns a screen that is scanned into a screen that has to be read, and the cost of missing one of them is a payment.

Print the arithmetic, do not imply it. Ordered, received, invoiced and the difference are four columns, and the difference is one of them rather than something the reader works out from the other three. Two people subtracting the same two figures in their heads get two answers often enough that the whole reconciliation is worth nothing, and the one who is wrong is the one who signs.

The direction of the subtraction is written into the column header — invoiced less received — because a signed figure with no stated direction is read both ways. A positive variance means the vendor billed for more than arrived; without the header sentence half the readers take it to mean the receipt was short, which is the same number and the opposite dispute.

Matching is a claim somebody is accountable for, not a gesture. The primary interaction is: select a record on one side with the arrow keys, choose from the candidates on the other, press the button that makes the pair. Drag is an accelerant layered over that and never the thing itself — HTML5 drag has no keyboard gesture anybody uses and does not fire on a touch screen, and a matching screen that can only be dragged cannot be operated by the accounts clerk on a tablet or by anybody using a keyboard. A pair is undone with an Unpair button until it is posted, and posting is a separate act with its own confirmation.

A variance row carries no stretched row link, and that is the one place this page deliberately does not copy table's linked-rows. A row here is not a record — it is two records and the difference between them — so a single anchor over the whole row has to pick one of them and lies about the other. The identifiers are separate anchors inside the first cell, which is two tab stops a row and is the honest cost of a row that is a pair.

A quantity column across mixed units does not total. MT, kg and nos do not add up, so the foot carries an em dash and the reason sits under the table. This is table/totals' rule and the answer is the same here, only more load-bearing: on a reconciliation a plausible wrong total in the foot is read as the finding.

An unmatched record is not a variance and the two must not be drawn as one thing. A receipt with no invoice against it means the invoice has not arrived, has not been posted, or has not been found, and only the last of those is work for this screen. Each side therefore states its own count and its own value and the two are never subtracted from each other — the figure that has to reach zero belongs to the bank reconciliation, where both sides really are the same account.

A match is an allocation with an amount, not a link between two ids. Store it as a link and neither of the two cases that actually turn up can be expressed: one invoice covering three receipts, and one receipt split across two invoices. Both are the same table read from opposite ends, both leave a remainder that has to be shown rather than rounded away, and a screen built on one-to-one pairing has to be rewritten the first week it meets a part shipment.

Three verdicts, and they wear the locked dots rather than a new palette: In tolerance takes emerald-600, Needs a reason takes amber-500, Blocked takes red-600. That is Closed, Approved and Overdue reading as finished, waiting on someone and the alarm state, which is what those three dots already mean. It is a reuse of the status table under different words and it is flagged for a person, on the same footing as record-page/states mapping On hold and Cancelled.

A line that cannot be posted offers no control at all. There is no reason box on a rate above the contract rate, because no reason makes it postable — what it needs is a credit note from the vendor or an amendment to the order, and neither is done from this screen. Giving it a reason field invites somebody to type a sentence and press a button that then refuses, and the refusal arrives after the work.

The post button is aria-disabled, never disabled, and the reason sits in a sentence the button is described by. disabled drops the one control somebody is hunting for out of the tab order with nothing to say why, and a browser moves focus off a disabled element to the body. The handler returns early instead, so the press is real and the refusal is announced.

Say when a difference is ordinary. A bank posts on value date and a ledger on voucher date, so the same payment sits on two dates one day apart, and an unannotated date column makes a clerk chase a variance that does not exist. The same goes for a cheque drawn and not presented: it is carried forward, it is not a difference, and the working has to distinguish the two or the reconciliation never closes.

Every figure carries tabular-nums and Indian digit grouping — ₹12,45,000, two-two-three above the last three digits. toLocaleString('en-IN') does it in the browser; on the server it is a project filter, because intcomma groups in threes and ₹1,245,000 is wrong by a factor of ten to anyone reading it at speed. Columns line up on the right so a variance stands out of a column without the digits being read.

An sr-only label carries its whole sentence in one string — a bare text node, or one x-text — never a run of nested spans. sr-only is position:absolute in a 1px box with overflow hidden, so an inline element inside it lays out past that box and reports a rect well beyond the right edge of a 390px screen. It is clipped and nothing scrolls, so it never shows up as a bug, but it trips every overflow audit the project will ever run. One string is also one accessible name rather than four fragments.

At 390px the table is not a table. A variance is four figures and a subtraction, so each line becomes a card whose arithmetic reads top to bottom as a small ledger with the difference ruled off under it, and the verdict moves from a column to a line under the figures. The agreeing lines move behind a segmented switch rather than into a second section, because a section four cards further down is not something anybody finds on a phone.

The page renders inside app-shell's main column and starts at <main>. The variants that need a bar stuck to the foot or a dialog over the page are shown in a bounded frame — h-[680px], rounded-xl, border-zinc-300 — so a whole screen previews in a box; as a real page, drop the height and the border, let the bar stick to the shell's scrolling column, and make the dialog fixed inset-0.

anatomy.description: page-header unchanged: breadcrumb, the one h1, which two documents are being reconciled, and the actions. Not sticky — the posting bar at the foot is what has to stay reachable.
The headline figures directly under the header: what each side says and the difference between them, at 20px, before any row is drawn. It is the answer to the question the page was opened with.
One line beside the band counting the lines into agree, in tolerance, needs a reason and blocked. Every number on it is derived from the same array the rows render from.

The exceptions, at full size. Ordered, received, invoiced, the difference in quantity, the difference in value, and the verdict. Header cells are table's, the numeric cells are right-aligned and tabular-nums, and below md it is stacked cards.

One line under the item name where the row is failing on an axis the columns do not carry — a rate above contract, a charge with no order line behind it. An alert-circle in red-600 and a sentence, never a field of colour.
badge's pill shape with the locked dot: emerald-600 in tolerance, amber-500 needs a reason, red-600 blocked. The word is in the pill, so the column reads without colour.
A tfoot on the recessed zinc-50 band. Each figure named by a th scope="row" in the column it totals, and the quantity column carrying an em dash because its units do not add.
The lines that match, collapsed to a count and their value, with a link that opens them. It is deliberately the smallest thing on the page.
One side of the two-sided view: a section with its own h2, its own count and its own value in the header, and the rows under it. The two panes are never subtracted from one another.
A fieldset of radios naming the record on the other side, each carrying the reason it is a candidate — same vendor, same value, dated two days apart — and a last option that means none of them.
The pairs made and not yet posted. A plain list, one Unpair button a row, and a line saying that nothing here has been written.
A receipt or an invoice with the amount of it allocated to the record on the other side, as a real input, with the remainder recomputed under the rows as an output.
shrink-0, opaque, top-bordered, stuck to the foot of the scrolling column: what is about to be written, in figures, and the one button that writes it.
An alertdialog that restates the figures — how many matches, what goes to the ledger, what is held back — and carries the amount on its confirm button.
One role="status" on the page root, in the document from first paint, for the changes focus does not announce: a pair made, a pair undone, a remainder that reached zero.

behaviour: The exceptions render first and the agreeing lines are a count. Nothing reorders on its own — the order is the order of the invoice, so a line found on the paper copy is found on the screen.

Every total, count and remainder is derived from the same array the rows render from, so the foot and the body cannot disagree. On a server-paged reconciliation the figures come from the server over the whole query and the label says which of the two it is.

Matching runs from the keyboard end to end. Arrow keys walk the unmatched list, Enter moves focus into the candidate set, the candidates are real radios, and one button makes the pair. Drag, where a project adds it, calls the same commit and adds nothing of its own.

A pair moves the record out of both unmatched lists and into the pairs list, moves the selection to the record that takes its place, moves focus with it, and says in the status region what was paired and how many are left.

The helper that reveals a selection focuses and scrolls and schedules nothing; whoever calls it decides when. Moving the selection is one tick. Making a pair is the frame after the tick, because the row is destroyed in one x-for iteration and created in another. Undoing one parks focus in the queue before it touches the arrays, because the button that was just pressed is the node about to be removed and a browser resets activeElement to the body the moment the focused node leaves the tree — restoring afterwards is a race against a teardown on a schedule nobody controls. All three failure modes measure as correct: the element is found, focus() is called, and the keyboard is on the document.

A pair is reversible until it is posted. Unpair returns both records to their lists at the index they left from and moves focus onto the restored one, because the button that was pressed no longer exists and focus would otherwise fall to the body. After posting there is no undo on this screen — a posted match is reversed by a journal, which is a separate approval, and the confirmation says so before the press.

A variance inside tolerance posts silently. One outside it will not post until a reason is chosen, and the posting bar says which line is holding it. One that cannot post at all offers no control and is excluded from the posting figures rather than blocking them.
Editing an allocation recomputes the remainder as it is typed. While the remainder is not zero the post button is aria-disabled and the sentence it is described by names the amount outstanding.

Posting is a separate act. The bar states what is about to be written, the dialog restates it in figures and carries the amount on its confirm button, and the submit is guarded rather than disabled while the request is in flight — the bar goes aria-busy and the button keeps focus and its width.

A reconciliation with nothing left is the clean state, and the view may only choose it when no filter is in force and the unscoped unmatched count is zero. It prints what was reconciled and what is carried into the next period, because a period closing does not mean nothing is open.
At 390px the exception table becomes one card a line, the two unmatched panes stack, and the agreeing lines move behind a segmented switch. Nothing scrolls sideways at any width.
accessibility: One main, one h1, and every region below it an h2 — the exceptions, the agreement, each side of the unmatched view, the pairs. The heading outline is the shape of the reconciliation and it is how anybody reads the page without a mouse.

The difference band is a description list: the label is the dt, the figure is the dd, and the sentence saying which way the subtraction runs sits with the figure rather than in a heading three lines above it.

Numeric cells are right-aligned and tabular-nums, and the identifying cell of a wide row is a th scope="row", so a variance eight columns along is announced with the line it belongs to rather than on its own.

A figure in the foot is named by a th scope="row" in the same row. A bare number at the bottom of a reconciliation is announced as a number with no word attached to it, which on this page is the worst place in the application for that to happen.

The unmatched list is a listbox with one Tab stop and a roving tabindex, exactly one option carrying aria-selected="true" and every other option carrying aria-selected="false". Nothing focusable goes inside an option; the controls that act on the selection live in the candidate set beside it.

The candidates are a real fieldset of radios named by a legend that carries the record being matched, so the group is announced as the destinations for that receipt rather than as four unrelated buttons. The last radio means none of them, because the only way to say none is an option that says so.

The guarded post button is aria-disabled="true" and stays focusable, with aria-describedby pointing at the sentence that names what is holding it. disabled would take the control out of the tab order with no explanation attached to anything.

The remainder is an <output> with aria-live="off", because it recomputes on every keystroke and an output is a live region by default. What announces a remainder reaching zero is the status region, once.

The status region is on the page root and is in the document before anything changes. It carries what focus cannot say — a pair made and the count left, a pair undone, a refusal from the server. A region rendered with its message already inside it has not changed and announces nothing.

The verdict is a word in the pill and the dot is aria-hidden, so a column of verdicts is readable without colour. The exception line states the reason in a sentence for the same reason: the red icon beside it is decoration and carries no label.

The confirmation is role="alertdialog" with aria-modal, a focus trap, and Escape closing it back onto the button that opened it. It does not dismiss on a backdrop click, because the question it asks has to be answered.
